children: Gold is approaching what could be a strong support zone after its sharp correction from record highs, making current levels increasingly attractive for investors, according to Lyn Alden, Founder of Lyn Alden Investment Strategy.

Alden believes the recent bounce in gold could be part of a broader recovery, although it may not necessarily mark the bottom. She remains bullish on the precious metal, saying prices are now at a fundamentally reasonable level.
On crude oil, Alden expects prices and refining margins to remain elevated over the next six months as markets assess the geopolitical implications of the Iran conflict.

However, she does not expect oil prices and refining spreads to revisit their recent highs during this period. She believes commodities are entering a more volatile phase, with geopolitical developments likely to influence price movements.

[faq type="interview" title="This is an edited transcript of the interview."][ques][/ques][ans][/ans][/faq][faq type="interview"][ques]We saw a sharp decline in crude and base metal prices over the last 10 to 15 days, followed by signs of recovery. Is the worst priced in, or should we expect another rally in the commodities arena?[/ques][ans]My expectation is we are probably entering a more choppy market. Once the United States (US) midterms entered in, the probability of continuation of the Iran war went down by some percentage. I think that alleviated, to some significant extent, the oil and refining market. Both oil is off its highs and importantly, crack spreads, basically the refining spreads compared to that crude oil, are off their highs. I don't expect to see those highs again in the next six months. But I do think they are probably going to remain elevated for the next six months as we still sort out what the actual geopolitical implications are. These still, of course, have investing implications globally.[/ans][/faq][faq type="interview"][ques]Gold prices are now at a 15-month low. Do you think there could be any upside, and is this a good time to buy?[/ques][ans]I do think that it is getting more bullish here. The two-year rise where it went to over 5,000 US dollars per ounce, the relative strength index on the monthly basis was the highest in our lifetimes. It was natural for that to correct. I think the 3,300 or 3,200 range is probably a support low. It doesn't mean that it can't go below that level, but it means that there is a lot of trading volume while it was rising to that level. I would be surprised to see it go below that level. I think that the current bounce that we are seeing, while it might not be the true low, is probably the lower band where if someone is still fundamental on gold as an asset class, is probably likely to want to get in here. I am personally bullish.[/ans][/faq][faq type="interview"][ques]Precious metals can go down very fast, but on the way up, the move is usually more measured compared to stocks. Do you agree?[/ques][ans]Usually. That is part of why the two-year bull run in gold was so surprising. It more than doubled in a two-year stretch, despite being a very large and liquid asset class. If you asked me two or three years ago would gold get as high as it did, I would say probably not. And then if you asked, would it correct as much, I would say probably not. But once it got that high, that is where the risks come in. If you go back a few years, gold at the current price is probably pretty reasonable compared to where it should be. If we can put aside the volatility of the past year or two, I think it is actually at a pretty fundamentally reasonable level, all things considered.[/ans][/faq]
